paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: giving is not a tax, it's a seed. Paul says, "Whoever sows generously will also reap generously" (2 Corinthians 9:6). And he says each one should give "what he has decided in his heart to give, not out of regret or compulsion. For God loves a cheerful giver" (2 Corinthians 9:7). So the question isn't how much can you squeeze out, it's whether your heart is in it.

Now why can a baker give cheerfully? Because the supply isn't coming from you. Paul says God is able to "make all grace abound to you," and that He is the One who "supplies seed to the sower and bread for food" (2 Corinthians 9:8, 10). I used to think my flour was MY flour, friend, and then I remembered who stocked the shelves. When the Source never runs dry, you can hold the cookie box with open hands.

And look where it goes. Paul says a gift like this meets needs and also overflows in "many expressions of thanksgiving to God" (2 Corinthians 9:12). People get helped, people pray, and God gets the glory. Paul ends it right where it all starts: "Thanks be to God for His indescribable gift!" (2 Corinthians 9:15). Every baker gives because Someone gave first, and that's a reason to smile.
